title: Chlorzoxazone in WWOX-LoF
summary: A preclinical comparison of early and late potassium feedback in WWOX-deficient cortex.

graph.evidence: First-spike AHP changes little in published Wwox means.
graph.inference: Train-evoked SK and BK effects remain unresolved.
graph.hypothesis: Slow SK feedback could restrain late spikes.
graph.experiment: Match calcium, then test first and late recruitment.

evidence: Mean first-spike afterhyperpolarization was 14.42 mV in juvenile Wwox knockout cortex versus 15.14 mV in controls. Train currents were not isolated. In a separate juvenile cortical model, increased BK current accompanied 46% more evoked spikes.
inference: Chlorzoxazone reduced Purkinje spike-interval variability at 30 µM and rat accumbens firing at 100 µM in an apamin-sensitive comparison. Transfer depends on cell type and exposure.
hypothesis: Reduced slow SK feedback could increase late spikes. Faster BK repolarization could instead increase early firing.
experiment: At matched calcium and voltage history, separate SK-sensitive and BK-sensitive train currents. Track early excitation, inhibitory recruitment and late recurrence at measured free exposure.
limits: Adolescent mean total plasma peaks were 53.1 and 29.5 µM. Unbound brain exposure is unresolved. Retain as a preclinical comparator and defer WWOX trial priority.
